messages:
ci-bot: PERF CHECK: microbench kv-read-latency failed on PR #5942 (> +30% threshold). Job: https://ci.redwood.ai/bench/kv-read-latency/5942 :warning:

alina: saw the CI alert. p50 jumped on the GPU perf runners (linux-gpu-small). Baseline p50=8.2ms -> PR p50=12.7ms. p95 also up.

jake: I can bisect this afternoon. Which commit range did the PR touch?

alina: PR touches kv cache eviction heuristics + a small kernel selector tweak. CI diff attached in job logs (see link above) — microbench shows consistent regression across 3 runs.

jake: starting bisect now. Running the bench locally to confirm: 

```
./ci/run_microbench.sh --bench=kv-read-latency --runs=50 --target=gpu
# output (local):
p50: 12.67ms p95: 28.1ms
```

jake: git bisect points to commit d4f7a3a (merge from branch optimize/kv-eviction, PR #5938). Commit message: "kv: prefer evicting completed batch slots to reduce mem churn".

priya: that was my change. I added logic to prefer completed batch slots to free contiguous ranges earlier — I expected more cache compaction and fewer allocations. Didn't expect a hit-rate regression.

alina: profiler shows a noticeable drop in KV cache hit rate for small-sequence workloads (sequence_length=32/64). From the benchmark traces: 

```
KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE (baseline): 0.72
KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE (after d4f7a3a): 0.49
# per-request avg load latency increased from ~0.85ms -> ~2.4ms
```

jake: digging into the eviction predicate: the new policy evicts contiguous ranges even if they contained partially-used entries. For our kernel-selector + small batch distribution that means the hot prefixes are getting torn out more often. The continuous batching heuristics were expecting higher hit rates for small prompts.

priya: hmm, I see. The change used an age threshold of 128 tokens to keep recently-used entries; maybe that's too coarse. I can try two options: (A) revert the change (fast) or (B) tweak predicate to prefer evicting only fully-empty ranges and lower age threshold for eviction.

dave: priority: this is a rollout blocker for the nightly canary. Please hold canary and any dedicated pool rollouts that include PR #5938.

ops-bot: Canary deployments paused: cluster redwood-eu-1 (auto-pause due to perf regression alert).

priya: opening emergency revert PR #5950 (revert d4f7a3a) and also prepping a follow-up #5951 with a less aggressive heuristic. ETA for revert review ~15m.

ci-bot: Triggered microbench run for PR #5950. See https://ci.redwood.ai/bench/kv-read-latency/5950.

ci-bot: microbench results for PR #5950 (revert): p50: 8.3ms p95: 19.2ms — within thresholds. All 3 runs stable. :white_check_mark:

alina: thanks — revert looks good. Approving #5950 now. After merge we should re-run the canary and monitor kv_hit_rate metric dashboard.

jake: left a comment on #5951: add a perf unit test that asserts kv_hit_rate for small sequence profiles doesn't drop below 0.65 relative to baseline, plus add a feature flag so we can A/B test the new eviction logic. Also add an integration trace tag: `kv_eviction_age_bucket` for easier dashboards.

priya: will push the smaller-patch approach in #5951 with tests and feature-flag. Sorry for the churn — the idea seemed safe in larger-batch sims but the microbench surfaced the small-batch edge.

dave: follow-ups: 1) include perf replay in PR checklist, 2) add a CI microbench gate for kv cache hit rate for future eviction changes, 3) add note to release notes and schedule 15m retrospective in tomorrow's eng-runtime sync.

alina: sounds good. After merge, I'm unpausing the canary and will watch the `kv_hit_rate` and `inference.p50` dashboards for the next 2 hours.

ops-bot: Canary resumed for cluster redwood-eu-1 (manual resume by alina).

jake: leaving a small postmortem comment on the revert PR describing the bisect steps and the profiling artifacts (nvprof traces + bench logs). We'll keep the bisect script at ./tools/perf/bisect_kernel_hit.sh for next time. :memo:

priya: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the safer heuristic PR and include the extra perf unit tests and a short benchmark summary in the PR description. :+1:

alina: closing the alert thread once metrics are stable. Great triage team work. :tada:
